tips.title: Dry Fitting: Use a Soft-Tip Pick to Remove Parts from the Mold
tips.text: Use a soft-tip pick to carefully remove parts from the mold, especially for resin or cast parts. This helps prevent damage to the part or the mold, and makes it easier to handle small, delicate components.

tips.title: Structural Support: Use 3M VHB Tape for Secure Attachments
tips.text: For attaching parts that require structural support, such as wings or fuselage sections, use 3M VHB (Vinyl-Coated, High-Bond) tape. This tape provides a strong, yet removable bond, and is suitable for a variety of materials, including plastic, metal, and wood.

tips.title: Modifying Parts: Use a Rotary Tool with a Carbide Bit for Precise Cutting
tips.text: When modifying parts, use a rotary tool (e.g., Dremel) with a carbide cutting bit. Carbide bits are designed for cutting through various materials, including plastic, metal, and wood, and provide a high level of precision and accuracy.

tips.title: Seam Filling: Use a Two-Part Epoxy for Strong, Flexible Bonds
tips.text: For filling seams, use a two-part epoxy (e.g., J-B Weld or 5-Minute Epoxy). These epoxies provide a strong, flexible bond that can withstand stress and fatigue, making them ideal for filling seams between parts that may be subject to movement or vibration.

tips.title: Construction Sequencing: Use a 'Build-Block' Approach for Efficient Assembly
tips.text: To optimize construction sequencing, use a 'build-block' approach. Identify key components or sub-assemblies and build these first, then integrate them into the larger assembly. This approach helps prevent mistakes, reduces the risk of damage, and ensures a more efficient build process.
